# Draft:Circassian conquest of the Central Caucasus (1502–1503)

The Circassian conquest of the Central Caucasus took place in 1502–1503. After the Crimean Khan Mengli I Giray destroyed the Great Horde, the Tatars who controlled the Central Caucasus were gone. The Circassians moved in and took the land. There was almost no fight. The Tatars were already beaten.
What happened
The Great Horde was the last remnant of the Golden Horde. It held parts of the North Caucasus, including the Central Caucasus region. After Mengli Giray crushed the Great Horde in 1502–1503, a power vacuum appeared. The Circassians saw their chance. They occupied the Central Caucasus.
The Circassians did not need to fight for the land. The Tatars had already been defeated by the Crimeans. The Circassians simply moved in and took control.
Aftermath
The Circassians (mostly Kabardians) ruled the Central Caucasus for the next 150 years. They became the main power in the region. Their control extended from the Kuban River to the Terek River. The Kabardian princes dominated the neighboring peoples: the Ossetians, the Ingush, and the Chechens.
The conquest also brought the Circassians into contact with the Nogais and the Crimeans. These relationships were often hostile. The Circassians fought many wars with the Nogai Horde and the Crimean Khanate for control of the North Caucasus.
